Claire / Mina — I reviewed the traffic sample and the model targets. Quick technical readout:

Summary:
- Uptime 99.99% (monthly) for a single dedicated pool is at the high end; achievable with an active-active multi-AZ deployment + automated failover, additional capacity reserved for burst (we generally size +25% headroom).
- Latency: p95 <= 100ms is achievable for shorter sequences (<=256 tokens) on rwd-7b optimized kernels with NVLink/GPU placement in the same AZ and local prefix caching. For longer sequences or chat-style sessions with big contexts, expect p95 to degrade; we recommend an explicit model-profiled SLO (e.g., p95 <=100ms for seq<=256; p95 <=200ms for seq<=1024).
- Failover RTO: <30s is realistic if customer accepts session rehydrate behavior (some requests will restart rather than resume streamed tokens). True connection-level session carry-forward is harder; we can document behavior.

Suggested order form language (technical clause to include):
- "Redwood will provide Dedicated inference capacity with Active-Active multi-AZ configuration sized to _X_ GPUs (as specified in the Order Form). Redwood targets a Monthly Uptime Percentage of 99.99% for the Dedicated Service when configured per the Active-Active specification and when Customer traffic profiles remain within the Order Form capacity sizing assumptions."
- "Latency SLOs will be model-and-sequence-length specific. For model family rwd-7b (seq<=256) Redwood targets p95 generation latency <= 100ms. For seq<=1024 performance targets are p95 <= 200ms. Performance guarantees are contingent on Customer routing, network egress latency, and payload sizes. See Appendix A (Performance Profiles) for profiling thresholds and test methodology."
- "Service credit schedule is tiered by minutes of unavailability per month; credits will be applied against the next invoice and capped at 25% of monthly fees for the affected service."

I'll attach a short tech appendix for Appendix A and propose the exact wording for the Order Form capacity table. If Claire can confirm the proportion of requests that are <=256 tokens we can lock the stricter p95 target.

-Jonas
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Mina / team — thanks. A few legal/commercial notes:

- 99.99% is a material commitment. We should insert a carve-out for scheduled maintenance windows and force majeure. Also want a clear definition for "Monthly Uptime Percentage" (standardize to minutes of unavailability / total minutes in billing month).
- Service credits: propose the following sliding scale we use often: 99.9–99.99 => 10% credit; 99.0–99.89 => 25%; <99.0 => 50% (examples; we can adjust). Cap credits at 25% unless exec approval.
- Latency guarantees should be tied to a measurable test harness in Appendix A with agreed sampling and ramp windows. Otherwise open-ended latency SLAs invite disputes. Recommend: include a profiling exercise clause — customer and Redwood run a 72-hour profile run; targets only apply after profile acceptance.

I'll prepare a redline of the MSA attachment and a draft addendum. If Procurement at Medisync insists on the 99.99 unconditional guarantee we should escalate to Sales Leadership for credit/levers approval.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel
Redwood Inference
